quotations.locator: §2, Theorem 2.1(i), opening hypotheses
quotations.quote_markdown: Let $X$ be a smooth, proper, geometrically connected curve over a number field; $D\subseteq X$ a reduced divisor; $U_X\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}X\backslash D$; $d$ a positive integer; $\epsilon\in\mathbb R_{>0}$ a positive real number. Write $\omega_X$ for the canonical sheaf on $X$. Suppose that $U_X$ is a hyperbolic curve — i.e., that the degree of the line bundle $\omega_X(D)$ is positive.

quotations.quote_markdown: We shall refer to the positive integer $v_K(q_E)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ as the local height of $E$ [or $E_K$].

quotations.locator: §3, Lemma 3.5, hypothesis concerning local heights and conclusion
quotations.quote_markdown:
Suppose further that $l$ is prime to the local heights of $E$ at all of its primes of [bad] multiplicative reduction [a condition that is satisfied, for instance, if $l$ is $>$ these local heights]. Then we have

$\frac{1}{12(1+\epsilon)}l\cdot\underline{\deg}_{\infty}(E)\leq\operatorname{ht}^{\mathrm{Falt}}(E)+2\log(l)+C$

for some constant $C\in\mathbb R$ which [may depend on $\epsilon$ but] is independent of $E$, $F$, $H_F$, and $l$.
quotations.scope_note: Final part of the lemma. Its preceding hypotheses include ε>0 and an l-cyclic subgroup scheme H_F⊆E_F. This excerpt is not the separate cyclic_bound field verbatim.
quotations.transcription: Manually transcribed from the original PDF and checked against the rendered pages in this task. Mathematical notation is transcribed as LaTeX.

quotations.locator: §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), paragraph beginning “Next, let us write”

$h\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})=\frac{1}{[F:\mathbb Q]}\cdot\sum_{v\in\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{non}}}h_v\cdot f_v\cdot\log(p_v)$

— that is to say, $h_v=0$ for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has good reduction; $h_v\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}$ is the local height of $E_F$ [cf. [GenEll], Definition 3.3] for those $v$ at which $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction.

quotations.locator: §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), (P4) and next display
quotations.quote_markdown:
(P4) $E_F$ does not admit an $l$-cyclic subgroup scheme.

Indeed, the existence of an $l$-cyclic subgroup scheme of $E_F$ would imply that

$\frac{l-2}{24}\cdot\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})\leq2\cdot\log(l)+T_{\mathcal K}$.
quotations.scope_note: Condition and beginning of its justification. The following paragraph obtains T_K from bounded discrepancies. The Lean cyclic_bound instead subtracts the contribution over 2 explicitly.
quotations.transcription: Manually transcribed from the original PDF and checked against the rendered pages in this task. Mathematical notation is transcribed as LaTeX.

quotations.locator: §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), (P5), (P6) and sentence after (P6)
quotations.quote_markdown:
(P5) if we write $\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}$ for the set of nonarchimedean valuations $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathbb V(F_{\mathrm{mod}})$ that do not divide $2l$ and at which $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction, then $\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}\neq\emptyset$.

[…] (P6) the image of the outer homomorphism $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/F)\to GL_2(\mathbb F_l)$ determined by the $l$-torsion points of $E_F$ contains the subgroup $SL_2(\mathbb F_l)\subseteq GL_2(\mathbb F_l)$.

Indeed, since, by (P5), $E_F$ has bad multiplicative reduction at some valuation $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}\neq\emptyset$, (P6) follows formally from (P2), (P4), and [GenEll], Lemma 3.1, (iii) [cf. the proof of the final portion of [GenEll], Theorem 3.8].
quotations.scope_note: Separate labeled conditions and final justification. The paragraph proving (P5) between the conditions is explicitly omitted.
quotations.transcription: Manually transcribed from the original PDF and checked against the rendered pages in this task. Mathematical notation is transcribed as LaTeX.

quotations.locator: §2, proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), (P7) and following paragraph
quotations.quote_markdown:
(P7) the resulting initial $\Theta$-data

$(\overline F/F,X_F,l,\underline C_K,\underline{\mathbb V},\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}},\underline\epsilon)$

satisfies the various conditions in the statement of Theorem 1.10.

Here, we note in passing that the crucial existence of data “$\underline{\mathbb V}$” and “$\underline\epsilon$” satisfying the requisite conditions follows, in essence, as a consequence of the fact [i.e., (P6)] that the Galois action on $l$-torsion points contains the full special linear group $SL_2(\mathbb F_l)$.
quotations.scope_note: Complete (P7) and next paragraph. The preceding paragraph invokes (P1), (P2), (P5), (P6) and [IUTchI], Definition 3.1(a)–(f). Underlines follow the PDF.
quotations.transcription: Manually transcribed from the original PDF and checked against the rendered pages in this task. Mathematical notation is transcribed as LaTeX.

— where we write

$\epsilon_E\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}(60\delta)^2\cdot\frac{\log(2\delta\cdot(\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall})))}{(\log(\mathfrak q^{\forall}))^{1/2}}$.

quotations.locator: §1, Definition 1.9(i), sentence defining normalized degree and pullback equality
quotations.quote_markdown:
If $\mathfrak a\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F)$, then we shall refer to

$$\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{1}{[F:\mathbb Q]}\cdot\deg_F(\mathfrak a)$$

as the normalized degree of $\mathfrak a$. Thus, for any finite extension $K$ of $F$, we have

$$\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a|_K)=\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a)$$

— where we write $\underline{\deg}(\mathfrak a|_K)$ for the normalized degree of the pull-back $\mathfrak a|_K\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(K)$ [defined in the evident fashion] of $\mathfrak a$ to $K$.
quotations.scope_note: Complete sentence(s) at the cited location.
quotations.transcription: Reused without changes from the previously verified paper-context.json. This task also checked rendered pp. 23–24; the original evidence remains the authority for pp. 21–22.

quotations.locator: §1, Definition 1.9(ii), opening through the definition of normalized E-degree
quotations.quote_markdown:
Let $v_{\mathbb Q}\in\mathbb V_{\mathbb Q}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\mathbb V(\mathbb Q)$, $E\subseteq\mathbb V(F)$ a nonempty set of elements lying over $v_{\mathbb Q}$. If $\mathfrak a=\sum_{v\in\mathbb V(F)}c_v\cdot v\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F)$, then we shall write

$$\mathfrak a_E\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\sum_{v\in E}c_v\cdot v\in\operatorname{ADiv}_{\mathbb R}(F);\qquad\underline{\deg}_E(\mathfrak a)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{\deg(\mathfrak a_E)}{\sum_{v\in E}[F_v:\mathbb Q_{v_{\mathbb Q}}]}$$

for the portion of $\mathfrak a$ supported in $E$ and the “normalized $E$-degree” of $\mathfrak a$, respectively.
quotations.scope_note: Complete sentence(s) at the cited location.
quotations.transcription: Reused without changes from the previously verified paper-context.json. This task also checked rendered pp. 23–24; the original evidence remains the authority for pp. 21–22.

quotations.locator: §1, Theorem 1.10, opening through the definition of the tripodal field
quotations.quote_markdown:
Fix a collection of initial $\Theta$-data as in [IUTchI], Definition 3.1. Suppose that we are in the situation of [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12, and that the elliptic curve $E_F$ has good reduction at every valuation $\in\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{good}}\cap\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{non}}$ that does not divide $2l$. In the notation of [IUTchI], Definition 3.1, let us write $d_{\mathrm{mod}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}[F_{\mathrm{mod}}:\mathbb Q]$, $(1\leq)\ e_{\mathrm{mod}}\ (\leq d_{\mathrm{mod}})$ for the maximal ramification index of $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ [i.e., of valuations $\in\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{non}}$] over $\mathbb Q$, $d_{\mathrm{mod}}^*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}2^{12}\cdot3^3\cdot5\cdot d_{\mathrm{mod}}$, $e_{\mathrm{mod}}^*\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}2^{12}\cdot3^3\cdot5\cdot e_{\mathrm{mod}}\ (\leq d_{\mathrm{mod}}^*)$, and

$$F_{\mathrm{mod}}\subseteq F_{\mathrm{tpd}}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}F_{\mathrm{mod}}(E_{F_{\mathrm{mod}}}[2])\subseteq F$$

for the “tripodal” intermediate field obtained from $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ by adjoining the fields of definition of the $2$-torsion points of any model of $E_F\times_F\overline F$ over $F_{\mathrm{mod}}$ [cf. Proposition 1.8, (ii), (iii)].
quotations.scope_note: The opening of the theorem. The further (3·5)-torsion and field-generation hypotheses follow on the same page and are outside this excerpt. They remain part of the paper theorem.
quotations.transcription: Reused without changes from the previously verified paper-context.json. This task also checked rendered pp. 23–24; the original evidence remains the authority for pp. 21–22.

quotations.locator: §1, Theorem 1.10 statement, sentence beginning “Here, we observe”
quotations.quote_markdown: Here, we observe that the various “$\log(q_{(-)})$”’s are independent of the choice of $F_{\square}$, and that the quantity “$\lvert\log(\underline{\underline q})\rvert\in\mathbb R_{>0}$” defined in [IUTchIII], Corollary 3.12, is equal to $\frac{1}{2l}\cdot\log(q)\in\mathbb R$ [cf. the definition of “$\underline q_{\underline v}$” in [IUTchI], Example 3.2, (iv)].
quotations.scope_note: Complete sentence(s) at the cited location.
quotations.transcription: Reused without changes from the previously verified paper-context.json. This task also checked rendered pp. 23–24; the original evidence remains the authority for pp. 21–22.

quotations.locator: §1, Theorem 1.10, first final displayed inequality
quotations.quote_markdown: $\frac16\cdot\log(\mathfrak q)\leq\left(1+\frac{20\cdot d_{\mathrm{mod}}}{l}\right)\cdot\left(\log(\mathfrak d^{F_{\mathrm{tpd}}})+\log(\mathfrak f^{F_{\mathrm{tpd}}})\right)+20\cdot(e_{\mathrm{mod}}^*\cdot l+\eta_{\mathrm{prm}})$
quotations.scope_note: First inequality in the theorem’s final displayed chain. Its next inequality replaces the tripodal-field invariants by the F-invariants. The theorem derives the chain under its full hypotheses on pp. 22–23.

definition_contexts.classification: Generic Lean interface motivated by the original paper; not a verbatim paper definition.

fields.name: Curve
fields.readback: A type intended to represent curve–divisor pairs (X,D).

fields.name: Pt
fields.readback: An algebraic-point type for each curve.

fields.name: Hyperbolic
fields.readback: A predicate intended to express positive log-canonical degree.

fields.name: DivisorFree
fields.readback: A predicate intended to express D=∅.

fields.name: ptLE
fields.readback: The degree-at-most subsets.

fields.name: ptEQ
fields.readback: The degree-exactly subsets.

fields.name: ptLE_zero
fields.readback: An interface law: the degree-at-most-zero set is empty.

fields.name: ptLE_succ
fields.readback: An interface law decomposing degree-at-most-(d+1).

fields.name: htCan
fields.readback: A real function intended as a representative of the log-canonical height class.

fields.name: logDiff
fields.readback: A real function intended as the normalized log-different.

fields.name: logCond
fields.readback: A real function intended as the normalized log-conductor.

fields.name: tripod
fields.readback: A distinguished curve intended as (P¹_Q,{0,1,∞}).

fields.name: hyperbolic_tripod
fields.readback: A witness that the distinguished curve satisfies Hyperbolic.

fields.name: CBS
fields.readback: A type intended to index the relevant compactly bounded subsets.

fields.name: cbsSet
fields.readback: The underlying point set for each CBS index.

definition_contexts.english_readback: This structure supplies an abstract height formalism. Its 15 fields name curves, point types, degree subsets, three real functions, the tripod, and compactly bounded subsets. It also supplies two degree-filter laws and a proof that the tripod is hyperbolic. These fields describe the intended geometric interpretation. The structure itself does not construct number fields, curves, divisors, heights, or local bounding domains.
definition_contexts.source_connection: Mochizuki reviews these objects in §1 of [GenEll] and uses them in Theorem 2.1, p. 11. The source code selects an interface sufficient to state that theorem.
limits: Curve and Pt are abstract types. Their geometric meanings come from the interpretation, not the bare types.
Hyperbolic and DivisorFree are predicates supplied by the interface.
The two degree-filter equations are explicit Lean interface laws. The paper defines degree subsets by fields and set difference.
CBS and cbsSet do not carry local domains or a named finite set Σ. The intended support condition is implicit in the choice of CBS.
No StatementI or StatementII theorem is part of the selected structure command.

definition_contexts.classification: Local auxiliary definitions that partition the total normalized height; not named definitions from the paper.
definition_contexts.english_readback: For local height data L, heightEq(q) sums the terms at bad places with residue characteristic q, then divides by L.deg. The function heightOther(a,b) sums the terms whose residue characteristics differ from both a and b, with the same denominator. Each term is hv(v)·f(v)·log(p(v)). These formulas partition the globally normalized height from IUT IV, p. 44.
definition_contexts.source_connection: Corollary 2.2(i), p. 41 separates all nonarchimedean primes from those away from 2. Condition (P5), p. 46 selects bad places away from 2l. Theorem 1.10, p. 23 defines its q-divisor on those selected bad places.
limits: heightOther(2,l) is identified with the theorem input log(q) only by the supplied thetaData equality. The generic sum definition alone proves no such geometric identification.
heightEq(q) keeps the global denominator deg. It is not Definition 1.9(ii)’s normalized E-degree, whose denominator sums local degrees over E.
The support sets can be empty. If a=b, the two exclusions coincide; a three-part decomposition requires a≠b.
The pilot quantity |log(q-underlined-underlined)| is log(q)/(2l), as stated in Theorem 1.10, p. 23. It must not be equated directly with heightOther(2,l).
definition_contexts.source_citation: Source context: IUT IV, Corollary 2.2(i), p. 41; proof of Corollary 2.2(ii), total-height paragraph on p. 44, (P5) on p. 46, and the first comparison on p. 47; Theorem 1.10, p. 23.

definition_contexts.classification: Generic Lean relations expressing the paper’s bounded-discrepancy notation.
definition_contexts.english_readback: DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s) means that some real C satisfies f(x)≤g(x)+C for every x in s. DiscrepancyEquiv(f,g,s) requires this bound in both directions. Thus the two functions differ by a bounded amount on s. The notation follows Mochizuki’s correction in IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1(ii), p. 55.
limits: The uncorrected direction printed in [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), p. 5 is reversed. Cite the correction when describing ≲.
The two directions may use different constants. A common absolute-value bound follows by taking their maximum.
These definitions introduce relations, not quotient types of BD-classes.
They apply to arbitrary real-valued functions on a type α. No geometric height theory is required to form the relations.

definition_contexts.english_readback: For an abstract height theory T, a compactly bounded index K, and a degree bound d, this structure supplies the height inputs for Corollary 2.2. Its 16 fields include local data, comparison bounds, finiteness properties, subgroup predicates, and an exceptional set. The conditions apply to points in T.cbsSet(K) of degree at most d, except htCan_equiv, which applies on all of T.cbsSet(K).
limits: The declaration does not prove that the 16 fields hold for a concrete elliptic-curve construction.

The source field cyclic_bound subtracts heightEq(2); the paper’s p. 45 display writes total log(q^∀) after bounded discrepancies. This is a local formulation of the needed bound, not the same printed formula.
The Lean B bounds the full contribution heightEq(2). The paper’s B_K on p. 47 bounds one sixth of the difference of the two heights. These constants have different normalizations.
TK has type ℝ without a positivity field. The local threshold uses max TK 0. The paper calls T_K positive on p. 45.
HasCyclicSubgroup, SL2Image, and excCore are supplied symbols. Their intended geometric meanings are not definitions proved by this structure.

definition_contexts.classification: Local proposition packaging the construction associated with (P7), plus formal interfaces and invariant comparisons. It is not a verbatim transcription of (P7).
definition_contexts.english_readback: Assume x lies in K, has degree at most d, and avoids the exceptional set. Let l be prime, with l≥7. Assume (P2), (P3), a bad place away from 2l, and the supplied SL2Image predicate. Then thetaData supplies a variant-data bundle X and its Theorem 1.10 invariants. The output satisfies P, its certificate, nonempty local estimates, X.l=l, and X.dmod≤d. It also identifies X.qPilot.logQ with heightOther(2,l) and gives the stated different and conductor comparisons.
limits: P, Corollary312VariantData, Theorem110Certificate, and LocalEstimate are repository interfaces. The paper does not use these Lean names or this conjunction.
The paper’s (P7), p. 46 says the constructed initial Θ-data satisfies Theorem 1.10. The local proposition packages that construction as an assumption to consume later.
The paper invokes (P1), (P2), (P5), and (P6) before (P7). The local input uses l≥7, (P2), (P3), the bad-place witness, and SL2Image. Do not claim these formulations are definitionally identical.
The final equality and two conductor inequalities correspond to p. 48. They are output fields of this assumption, not new proofs in this definition.
X.qPilot.logQ is the repository’s Theorem 1.10 log(q) carrier. The separately normalized Corollary 3.12 pilot log-volume includes the factor 1/(2l).

definition_contexts.classification: Local explicit sufficient threshold. The formula is not printed in Mochizuki’s paper.
definition_contexts.english_readback: This local function takes the maximum of four bounds. They support the prime-selection threshold, the cyclic-subgroup exclusion, the bad-place existence argument, and ε_E≤1. The paper instead enlarges a finite exceptional set at these steps. The fourth powers and the displayed constants are choices in the Lean implementation.
limits: This numeric definition alone proves none of the four consequences. Later arguments must use the input hypotheses.
This formula is not the paper’s full quantitative exceptional-set bound H_unif·ε_d^(-3)·d^(4+ε_d)+H_K. It must not be described as an equivalent statement of Corollary 2.2(ii) or (iii).
